images.title: Pont du Gard BLS.jpg
images.description: Pont du Gard , in Vers-Pont-du-Gard, Gard department, South France. The Pont du Gard is the most famous part of the roman aqueduct which carried water from Uzès to Nîmes until roughly the 9th century when maintenance was abandoned. The monument is 49m high and now 275m long (it was 360m when intact) at its top. It's the highest roman aqueduct, but also one of the best preserved (with the aqueduct of Segovia). The Pont du Gard has been a UNESCO world heritage site since 1985.

images.title: Le jardin d'eau de Claude Monet (Giverny) (48751405171).jpg
images.description: Amateur d'art japonais et de jardins, le peintre impressionniste Claude Monet a étendu le terrain de sa maison de Giverny en 1893 pour y créer un jardin d'eau, planté de nombreux végétaux dont des nénuphars. Il y a fait construire un pont japonais qu'il a fait peindre en vert pour se démarquer de la tradition des jardins japonais. Ce jardin d'eau a été pour lui une importante source d'inspiration, il est à l'origine de la série de ses tableaux Nymphéas, donnés par le peintre à la France en 1918 comme symbole de la paix. Ils sont exposés dès 1927 au musée de l'Orangerie à Paris. Ce musée a été créé par l'État français, sous l'impulsion de Georges Clémenceau, grand ami de Claude Monet. www.musee-orangerie.fr/fr/article/lensemble-de-lorangerie Le jardin d'eau sur le site de la Fondation Monet fondation-monet.com/giverny/le-jardin-deau/ Le Bassin aux nymphéas de Claude Monet au Musée d'Orsay, Paris (photo dalbera) www.flickr.com/photos/dalbera/48704550181/in/album-721576...

images.title: Bonnieux - Eglise Neuve.jpg
images.description: After Lourmarin, our first photo stop was above the picturesque village of Bonnieux in The Luberon. It has a church at the centre of the village and a nice view of the Luberon countryside. Bonnieux is one of the Luberon's most attractive villages. It tilts gently down the north-westerly slope of the Luberon. Its control over the access to the river Durance and its political importance gave it a privileged status, whilst its relative geographical isolation protected it from the various scourages of these troubled times (it was only moderately affected by the ravages of the plague). The village started to grow by the churchside at the top of the promontory and gradually followed the slope down to where the new church is. The concentric levels are linked up by picturesque alleyways bordered with elegant houses. Our tour guide mentioned that the tiles of the rooftops were made by forming them over peoples legs and knees! The church in these shots is the new church. Church dating from the nineteenth century (1870), contains four primitive sixteenth century from the Old Church and scenes from the Passion.
